doc: Bluesky / ATProto content, read-only: one message, a conversation, an account. Renders from plain ATProto-shaped data — no network of its own and no clock; the pictures it draws and the links it offers are the two origins its views name.

capabilities.reason: avatars, banners and image thumbnails from cdn.bsky.app, and profile / hashtag / permalink links to bsky.app. Both origins are literals in the views; the records only ever supply the path.

components.name: Scope
components.doc: What the answer beside it does NOT cover: a cap that stopped it, a page nobody read, an index that only holds part of the world. Not an error and not a warning — the sentence that turns a count into a claim a reader can check.

messageDocs.name: summary
messageDocs.doc: Everything this scope discloses, as one line — the card's tooltip.

messageDocs.name: hasAny
messageDocs.doc: Whether there is anything to disclose at all. A scope with nothing to say draws nothing.

messageDocs.name: truncatedLabel
messageDocs.doc: What stopped the answer early, spelled out.

messageDocs.name: moreLabel
messageDocs.doc: That another page existed and was not read.

fields.name: truncated
fields.doc: A cap stopped this before the data ran out. The field that matters most: it is the difference between "there is no more" and "I stopped looking".

fields.name: truncatedBy
fields.doc: What stopped it, in the caller's own words — `limit`, `depth`.

fields.name: more
fields.doc: There is another page, and nobody asked for it.

fields.name: notes
fields.doc: What this answer does not cover, one sentence each. Free text because the reasons are not a closed set: an index that only holds recent public posts and a filter the service applied are both true and neither is a boolean.

inits.name: a search that stopped early
inits.argsJson: {"truncated": true, "truncatedBy": "limit", "more": true, "notes": ["search indexes recent public posts only", "accounts that block this one are not in the index"]}
inits.doc: The shape a partial answer takes: a cap, an unread page and two things the index itself does not hold.

inits.name: a capped conversation
inits.argsJson: {"truncated": true, "truncatedBy": "depth", "notes": ["replies deeper than the requested depth were not fetched", "deleted and blocked messages are named in the text, not drawn here"]}
inits.doc: What a thread leaves out, which is where a card looks most complete and is least so.

components.name: Post
components.doc: One bluesky message: who wrote it, what it says (with its facets resolved), what it carries and how it was received. Also the row a Thread and a Profile are made of.

messageDocs.name: toggleLike
messageDocs.doc: Like this message, or take the like back. Optimistic: the count moves here and a `liked` / `unliked` bubble says so.

messageDocs.name: toggleRepost
messageDocs.doc: Repost this message, or take the repost back.

messageDocs.name: toggleFold
messageDocs.doc: Fold the replies under this message away, or bring them back. Only a row inside a thread has any.

messageDocs.name: liked
messageDocs.doc: This reader liked the message; carries its uri.

messageDocs.name: unliked
messageDocs.doc: This reader took a like back; carries its uri.

messageDocs.name: reposted
messageDocs.doc: This reader reposted the message; carries its uri.

messageDocs.name: unreposted
messageDocs.doc: This reader took a repost back; carries its uri.

messageDocs.name: summary
messageDocs.doc: The author and the three counts, as one sentence.

messageDocs.name: folded
messageDocs.doc: This row folded its replies away; carries its uri. The row keeps the flag; the thread above is what knows which messages stop rendering because of it.

messageDocs.name: unfolded
messageDocs.doc: This row brought its replies back; carries its uri.

messageDocs.name: foldTitle
messageDocs.doc: What the fold button will do, spelled out — its label is a glyph.

messageDocs.name: owned
messageDocs.doc: Set by whoever builds a row; it draws smaller and sits inside their list.

messageDocs.name: repostLabel
messageDocs.doc: Who put this message in front of this reader, spelled out.

messageDocs.name: labelTitle
messageDocs.doc: Every label on the record, as one sentence — the chip row's tooltip.

fields.name: uri
fields.doc: The record's at:// uri (at://<did>/app.bsky.feed.post/<rkey>), which the permalink is derived from.

fields.name: displayName
fields.doc: The author's display name; the handle stands in when it is empty.

fields.name: handle
fields.doc: The author's handle, without the leading @.

fields.name: text
fields.doc: What the message says.

fields.name: createdAt
fields.doc: When it was written, as an ISO 8601 stamp.

fields.name: avatar
fields.doc: The author's picture, as the full url the record carries. Drawn when it is on cdn.bsky.app — the origin the view names — and the initials show through when it is not.

fields.name: facets
fields.doc: Rich-text ranges: { byteStart, byteEnd, kind: link|mention|tag, value }. The offsets are UTF-8 byte offsets, as on the wire.

fields.name: images
fields.doc: Attached images as { alt, thumb }. The thumbnail is drawn when it is on cdn.bsky.app; an image without one is its alt text on a chip, which is what every image was before this bundle could load any.

fields.name: replyCount
fields.doc: How many replies the record came with.

fields.name: repostCount
fields.doc: How many reposts the record came with.

fields.name: likeCount
fields.doc: How many likes the record came with.

fields.name: liked
fields.doc: Whether this reader has liked it, counted on top of likeCount.

fields.name: reposted
fields.doc: Whether this reader has reposted it, counted on top of repostCount.

fields.name: depth
fields.doc: How deep in a reply tree this message sits; 0 stands on its own. Drawn as that many rails, since an untrusted view has no style attribute to indent with.

fields.name: focus
fields.doc: Whether this is the message its thread is about; marks the card.

fields.name: foldable
fields.doc: How many replies sit under this one in the thread that built it. 0 hides the fold button.

fields.name: folded
fields.doc: Whether this reader folded those replies away.

fields.name: owned
fields.doc: Whether this message is a row inside a larger surface — a thread, a feed — rather than standing on its own. A row draws smaller. It keeps its own like / repost / fold either way.

fields.name: repostedBy
fields.doc: The handle of the account that reposted this message into the feed it arrived in; empty when nobody did. Drawn as a line ABOVE the card — the author is never rewritten, because the message is still the message.

fields.name: pinned
fields.doc: Whether the feed this arrived in had it pinned to the top.

fields.name: labels
fields.doc: Moderation label values on the record (`porn`, `graphic-media`, `!warn`, …), as the labellers set them. Named, never acted on: which labels mean "hide this" depends on the reader's own preferences and on which labellers they subscribe to, and neither is in this bundle's reach.

fields.name: external
fields.doc: An unfurled link, as `{ uri, title, description, thumb }`. The uri is a target and never a link — the poster chose that origin, so no view can name it — while the thumbnail is re-hosted by the AppView and is drawn when it is on cdn.bsky.app.

fields.name: quote
fields.doc: The quoted message, as `{ uri, displayName, handle, avatar, text, createdAt }`. Flat and plain: a quote's own rich text would need a loop inside a loop, which a static view cannot do, so its permalink is under it for whoever wants the real thing.

fields.name: video
fields.doc: An attached video, as `{ thumb, alt }`. There is no player — a playlist is a fetch this bundle cannot make — so a video is its poster frame on the CDN and its alt text.

components.name: Feed
components.doc: A list of messages that is not a conversation: a timeline, one account's posts, a page of search results. Each row is a Post standing on its own — no reply rails, nothing to fold — with a Scope under it saying what the page left out.

messageDocs.name: title
messageDocs.doc: The heading, set by whoever built the list.

messageDocs.name: summary
messageDocs.doc: How many messages there are, and how many of them somebody reposted in.

messageDocs.name: liked
messageDocs.doc: A row was liked. The row keeps the flag; the bubble travels on, because only the component above can write to a PDS.

messageDocs.name: unliked
messageDocs.doc: A row's like was taken back.

messageDocs.name: reposted
messageDocs.doc: A row was reposted.

messageDocs.name: unreposted
messageDocs.doc: A row's repost was taken back.

fields.name: title
fields.doc: What this list IS — "@bsky.app — posts and replies", `search: "wasm"`. A feed is the one surface here that cannot say what it is from its own contents: three flat messages are three flat messages whether they came from a timeline, an author or a search, so whoever asked for them is the one who says. Empty leaves the summary line standing on its own.

fields.name: posts
fields.doc: The messages, in the order the service returned them. Same record shape a Thread's posts take, minus the reply structure: every row is at depth 0 because a feed is a list, and `repostedBy` / `pinned` say why each one is here.

fields.name: scope
fields.doc: What this page does not cover. Written as a plain record — the keys are the Scope component's own field names — and drawn only when there is something to disclose.

components.name: Thread
components.doc: A conversation: the messages of a reply tree, flattened and indented by depth, each rendered as a Post of its own, with any subtree foldable.

messageDocs.name: folded
messageDocs.doc: A row folded its replies away — the thread is what knows which rows those are, so it drops them and stops the bubble here.

messageDocs.name: unfolded
messageDocs.doc: A row brought its replies back.

messageDocs.name: liked
messageDocs.doc: A row was liked. The thread keeps the flag for that row and hands the row back rebuilt, then lets the bubble travel on: only the component above can write to a PDS.

messageDocs.name: unliked
messageDocs.doc: A row's like was taken back.

messageDocs.name: reposted
messageDocs.doc: A row was reposted.

messageDocs.name: unreposted
messageDocs.doc: A row's repost was taken back.

messageDocs.name: summary
messageDocs.doc: How many messages there are, and how many are folded away.

fields.name: posts
fields.doc: The conversation in reading order, each message { uri, displayName, handle, avatar, text, createdAt, facets, images, replyCount, repostCount, likeCount, depth } — depth being how deep in the reply tree it sits.

fields.name: focus
fields.doc: The uri of the message the thread is about; that row is marked. Empty for none. Writing it rebuilds the rows.

fields.name: scope
fields.doc: What this conversation does not show — the depth the caller asked for and the one the service applied. Written as a plain record whose keys are the Scope component's own field names.

components.name: Profile
components.doc: One account: who it is, what it says about itself, its three counts, and its recent messages.

messageDocs.name: toggleFollow
messageDocs.doc: Follow this account, or unfollow it. Optimistic, and announced as a bubble.

messageDocs.name: followed
messageDocs.doc: This reader followed the account; carries its handle.

messageDocs.name: unfollowed
messageDocs.doc: This reader unfollowed the account; carries its handle.

messageDocs.name: summary
messageDocs.doc: The account and its counts, as one sentence.

messageDocs.name: followLabel
messageDocs.doc: What the follow button says right now.

messageDocs.name: liked
messageDocs.doc: A message in the feed was liked; the profile keeps the flag for that row, as a thread does.

messageDocs.name: unliked
messageDocs.doc: A message's like was taken back.

messageDocs.name: reposted
messageDocs.doc: A message in the feed was reposted.

messageDocs.name: unreposted
messageDocs.doc: A message's repost was taken back.

messageDocs.name: joinedLabel
messageDocs.doc: When the account was created, as a date a person reads.

fields.name: displayName
fields.doc: The account's display name; the handle stands in when it is empty.

fields.name: handle
fields.doc: The account's handle, without the leading @.

fields.name: description
fields.doc: The account's own description of itself.

fields.name: avatar
fields.doc: The account's picture, as the full url the record carries. Drawn when it is on cdn.bsky.app; the initials show through when it is not.

fields.name: banner
fields.doc: The strip behind the picture, as the full url the record carries. Same rule as the avatar, and a flat band of base-200 when there is none.

fields.name: followersCount
fields.doc: How many accounts follow it.

fields.name: followsCount
fields.doc: How many accounts it follows.

fields.name: postsCount
fields.doc: How many messages it has written.

fields.name: following
fields.doc: Whether this reader follows it, counted on top of followersCount.

fields.name: posts
fields.doc: Its recent messages, in the same shape a Thread's posts take; each becomes a Post of its own, standing on its own (no depth, nothing to fold).

fields.name: createdAt
fields.doc: When the account was created, as an ISO 8601 stamp. Drawn as a date and not a duration: "3 years ago" needs a clock, and this bundle asks for no `cap-clock`.

fields.name: pinnedPost
fields.doc: The at:// uri of the message this account pinned to its profile. The uri and not the message: `getProfiles` answers with a strong ref, so the content is one more request away and this bundle makes none — what a card can honestly offer is the link.
